bullets.title: Long-end yields surge to multi-decade highs; macro backdrop turns hawkish
bullets.body: The 30-year US Treasury yield hit 5.31%, its highest since June 2007, and the 10-year reached 4.75%, a 19-month high. Japan's 30-year yield spiked to a record 4.05%, Germany's hit its highest since 2011, and South Korea's 30-year reached a record 4.79%. Goldman's Delta-One desk warned the Fed could be forced to hike, while Yardeni identified 5% on the 10-year as the key threshold where problems could emerge. JPM notes long-end yields moved higher on global factors with 30Y approaching post-2007 highs.

bullets.title: Tech-led selloff dominates tape; semis -5%, semiconductors break 50-day MA
bullets.body: The S&P 500 IT Index closed -1.9% and semiconductors fell 5%, with memory, semi-cap equipment, CPU, and AI names dragging. SOXX broke below its 50-day moving average after failing to clear resistance the prior day. JPM attributed the selling to low summer volume and lack of catalysts rather than structural de-risking, noting SOXX remains ~18% above July lows and positioning is still only at the 40th percentile. NVDA bore the most bearish options flow of any stock on the day.

bullets.title: Market increasingly dependent on 'Goldilocks' macro; hedging demand rising despite stable prices
bullets.body: Multiple indicators flag growing divergence between stable price action and rising tail-risk hedging: skew is getting bid, hyperscaler CDS is widening, and downside convexity is building while headline vol remains suppressed. One observer noted an inverse correlation between AI infrastructure and SaaS rallies that appears designed to unwind long-GAI/short-SaaS institutional positions. The Fear & Greed index sits at neutral 55/100, and a $2.3B SPY put wall at 765 and a $1B QQQ put wall at 720 are notable technical levels.

bullets.title: July macro data broadly weak: housing starts plunge 12.4%, pending home sales miss
bullets.body: July housing starts fell 12.4% m/m to 1.239M SAAR (vs. 1.350M estimate), approaching COVID-era lows and hitting the weakest single-family level since November 2022. Pending home sales dropped 2.3% m/m vs. a flat consensus, lowest since January, as mortgage rates and record prices weighed. Building permits beat at 1.443M vs. 1.370M estimate—the only bright spot. July import prices fell 0.4% m/m (est. +0.1%) and export prices dropped 1.3% m/m (est. flat). Industrial production rose a below-consensus 0.2%.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risk escalates: Iran fires ballistic missiles at UAE, Strait of Hormuz tensions persist
bullets.body: UAE detected two Iranian ballistic missiles, with one intercepted and one landing outside territorial waters, prompting emergency alerts in Dubai. Iran's FM rejected ceasefire proposals and the country announced Hormuz would remain closed, though Trump subsequently claimed all mines were removed or detonated and denied active Iran negotiations. US diesel refining margins hit a record $102/barrel on supply disruption fears, crude futures rose >$1, and retail diesel prices jumped 3.7% to $5.45/gal in the past week.

bullets.title: US-Canada tariff deadline approaching; negotiators expected to meet before midnight
bullets.body: Canadian and US negotiators are expected to hold talks ahead of a midnight tariff deadline, keeping trade policy uncertainty elevated.

bullets.title: Private credit stress at decade highs; Delaware Life cuts $6.5B affiliated investments
bullets.body: The FT reports private credit distress metrics at 10-year highs with strain spreading sector-wide. Delaware Life, a life insurer with ties to AI SPV funding structures, was ordered to cut $6.5B in affiliated investments. One commentator noted AI SPVs rely heavily on life insurance/private credit pipelines, raising concerns about the funding supply for hyperscaler infrastructure deals. Investment-grade bond spreads are also widening per Roger Altman's comments.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole (Aug 28) and NVDA earnings (Aug 26) are next key catalysts
bullets.body: JPM maintains a Tactical Bullish view and sees dip-buying opportunities with NVDA earnings on August 26 and Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on August 28 as the next major inflection points. VIX expires Wednesday, and multiple vol indicators (VVIX, COR1M) sit at lows, suggesting near-term vol support will persist through next week before depending on Fed communications.

bullets.title: Anthropic raises $10B+ pre-IPO credit facility; valuation at ~$65B
bullets.body: Anthropic's pre-IPO revolving credit facility is set to climb past its $10B target, with lead banks asked to lend ~$1.25B each and next-tier lenders ~$1B each, implying a ~$65B valuation. Prediction markets assign 44% odds to an Anthropic IPO exceeding SpaceX's valuation. Separately, one commentator noted Anthropic's $65B ARR figure (vs. $75-80B implied by some) was the catalyst JPM cited for Tuesday's tech selloff, though they attributed it to low-volume summer dynamics.

bullets.title: Big Tech AI capex balloon includes ~$3T in off-balance-sheet commitments
bullets.body: Per analysis circulating on X, nine major tech companies have approximately $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet AI-related spending commitments, dramatically understating reported capex figures. Hyperscalers' debt issuance is also approaching the scale of major banks in the investment-grade bond market. NVDA is backing a $105B SoftBank data center in Ohio (scaled back from $250B), and Amazon expanded its Louisiana data center investment from $12B to $18B.

bullets.title: Texas data center moratorium creates hyperscale demand displacement risk
bullets.body: Texas Governor Abbott's August 3 audit order effectively froze new ERCOT grid connections, affecting 1,800+ projects representing 474 GW of queued capacity—~90% from data centers. Texas is the country's fastest-growing data center market, and the state legislature won't reconvene until January 2027, limiting near-term policy changes. At least 18-30 states are restricting or considering restrictions on data center development, potentially forcing hyperscale demand to other regions.

bullets.title: ARM cloud instances +41% YoY; Blackwell GPUs +31% m/m as server growth continues
bullets.body: Keybank's Cloud Instance Tracker shows total cloud instances up +2% m/m and +14% y/y in July. ARM drove the headline at +4% m/m and +41% y/y (Google Axion +10% m/m, AWS Graviton +5% m/m). NVDA instances rose +2% m/m / +10% y/y with Blackwell up +31% m/m to 333 instances. INTC Granite Rapids gained +10% m/m to 4,145 instances. AMD was flat m/m. Keybank views the data as positive for ARM, INTC, MU, and NVDA; neutral for AMD.

bullets.title: US retail web traffic decelerates in August Week 2 but remains strong on MTD basis
bullets.body: Citi's tracker shows US retail web traffic averaged +29.8% in August Week 2, down from +32.1% in Week 1, with weather acting as a ~1.8°F YoY drag. August Week 3 is forecast ~4°F warmer YoY which should provide a tailwind. MTD traffic +30.8% avg, similar to July's pace. Dick's Sporting Goods leads at +47% MTD, Target +44%, Walmart +15%. WOOF decelerated sharply to +low-20s from +low-70s in July.

bullets.title: Treasury 20-year auction Wednesday seen requiring deeper concession
bullets.body: JPM expects tomorrow's $16B 20-year bond auction to need more concession given rich valuations and unattractive macro backdrop. The July auction cleared 0.5bp cheap with end-user demand at a multi-month low of 85.3%; investment manager takedown fell 9.9 ppts to 67.5%. 20-year yields are up 12bp since the last auction and at levels last seen in October 2023.

bullets.title: Apple announces EU App Store overhaul; replaces Core Tech Fee with 5% external transaction commission
bullets.body: Effective October 1, Apple is restructuring EU App Store fees: in-app purchases will carry a 26% commission, alternative payment methods 20%, apps linking to external purchases 15%, and a new 5% commission on digital transactions outside the App Store replaces the Core Technology Fee. The changes include expanded access to alternative app marketplaces and new child safety protections for users under 13.

bullets.title: META down 4.4%+ on day as 29-state youth mental health trial commences
bullets.body: Federal court trial began Tuesday with prosecutors from 29 states alleging Meta deliberately hooked and exploited children on Instagram and Facebook. META has spent most of 2026 below its 200-day moving average, making 2026 its worst year since 2022's 74% decline. Shares are down over 16% YTD and hit two-week lows intraday. JPM attributed some of the weakness to off-balance-sheet financing press as well as the trial headline.

bullets.title: Global bond selloff pressure: investors positioning for stagflation, BofA survey shows
bullets.body: BofA's latest fund manager survey shows investors bracing for stagflation over the next 12 months even as the same survey reflects bullishness on US equities. The Cleveland Fed's business survey shows executives expect 3.3% CPI (down from 3.7% in Q2) with stable 2.8% wage growth. NY Fed Services PMI slumped to +0.5 in August from +8.7 prior, with the business climate index at -25.7 and prices paid accelerating to 70.1.

bullets.title: ANET guides 40% 2026 revenue growth; sees $20B Ethernet AI networking market by 2030
bullets.body: At the Rosenblatt Technology Summit, Arista guided 40% revenue growth for 2026 with potential upside if supply improves. The 1.6 Tbps platform enters volume production in 2027 with a $20B scale-up networking opportunity by 2030 and material revenue impact from 2028. Gross margin guided at 60-64% for 2027; operating margin 48-49% for 2026. Campus business growing 45-50% in 2026.

bullets.title: US hotel RevPAR remains robust; July global figures show US +8.2% YoY
bullets.body: July global hotel RevPAR was strong with US at +8.2% YoY (maintaining near-June's +8.4%), luxury chain-scale up +17.7% (best since January 2023), and economy segment positive for a fourth consecutive month at +3.6%. Middle East contracted -11.3% (Dubai -26%) on Iran-related conflict escalation. Week ending August 15 showed US RevPAR +6.1% YoY with economy segment accelerating vs. prior week despite harder comps.

bullets.title: Google accelerates China supply chain exit; Pixel production moves to Vietnam/India by 2027
bullets.body: Google is reportedly planning to move its entire Pixel smartphone, watch, and earbud supply chain out of China by 2027, with Vietnam and India as primary destinations. The move is part of broader US tech de-risking from China amid geopolitical pressure; US Congress is simultaneously pushing Apple to sign a written pledge not to use Chinese memory chips.
